overview.summary: This chapter examines the autonomous electoral machinery that sustains Indian democracy. It explores the constitutional mandate of the Election Commission under Article 324, traces the pioneering contributions of first Chief Election Commissioner Sukumar Sen and first voter Shyam Sharan Negi, outlines the sequential stages of elections from delimitation to counting, discusses the Model Code of Conduct, and proposes crucial electoral reforms.
youWillLearn: Understand the constitutional status and powers of the Election Commission of India
Learn the roles of first Chief Election Commissioner Sukumar Sen and first voter Shyam Sharan Negi
Trace the full sequential lifecycle of an election from delimitation to declaration of results
Examine how the Delimitation Commission and Model Code of Conduct ensure fair play
Identify modern electoral reforms including EVM-VVPAT technology and curbing criminalisation

notes.title: Political Party
notes.question: Explain the following concept: Political Party
notes.qnaAnswer:
1. A political party is a group of people who come together to contest elections and hold power in the government.
2. It has a specific ideology, policies, and programs.
3. It aims to promote the collective good and the interests of its members.
4. It has a leader, an active member base, and a support base among the people.
5. It plays an important role in a democracy by providing a link between the government and the people.

notes.title: National Party
notes.question: Explain the following concept: National Party
notes.qnaAnswer:
1. A national party is a political party that is recognized as such by the Election Commission of India.
2. It has a presence in multiple states and a significant vote share across the country.
3. It has a national-level organization and leadership.
4. Examples: Indian National Congress, Bharatiya Janata Party, Communist Party of India.
5. National parties play an important role in national politics and governance.

notes.title: Regional Party
notes.question: Explain the following concept: Regional Party
notes.qnaAnswer:
1. A regional party is a political party that is active in a specific region or state.
2. It focuses on regional issues and interests.
3. It is recognized as a state party by the Election Commission of India.
4. Examples: Shiv Sena (Maharashtra), DMK (Tamil Nadu), Akali Dal (Punjab).
5. Regional parties play an important role in state politics and coalition governments.

notes.title: Short Note: Indian National Congress
notes.question: Write a short note on: Indian National Congress
notes.qnaAnswer:
1. The Indian National Congress (INC) was founded in 1885.
2. It played a leading role in the Indian freedom struggle.
3. After independence, it became a major political party in India.
4. It has been in power at the centre for many years.
5. Its ideology is based on secularism, socialism, and democracy.

notes.title: Short Note: Bharatiya Janata Party
notes.question: Write a short note on: Bharatiya Janata Party
notes.qnaAnswer:
1. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) was founded in 1980.
2. It is one of the major national parties in India.
3. Its ideology is based on Hindutva, nationalism, and cultural conservatism.
4. It has been in power at the centre since 2014.
5. It has a strong organizational base across the country.

notes.title: Short Note: Shiv Sena
notes.question: Write a short note on: Shiv Sena
notes.qnaAnswer:
1. Shiv Sena is a regional political party in Maharashtra.
2. It was founded in 1966 by Bal Thackeray.
3. It focuses on Marathi identity and regional issues.
4. It has been a major political force in Maharashtra.
5. It has been part of both state and central governments.

notes.title: Short Note: Functions of Political Parties
notes.question: Write a short note on: Functions of Political Parties
notes.qnaAnswer:
1. Contesting elections and forming governments.
2. Making policies and programs.
3. Providing a link between the government and the people.
4. Articulating and aggregating interests.
5. Socializing and mobilizing citizens.
6. Providing leadership and recruiting political leaders.

notes.title: Characteristics of Political Parties
notes.question: Explain the characteristics of political parties.
notes.qnaAnswer:
1. A political party is a group of people who come together to contest elections.
2. It has a specific ideology and policies.
3. It aims to promote the collective good.
4. It has a leader and an active member base.
5. It has a support base among the people.
6. It plays an important role in a democracy.

notes.title: Role of Political Parties in Democracy
notes.question: Explain the role of political parties in democracy.
notes.qnaAnswer:
1. Political parties contest elections and form governments.
2. They make policies and programs for the welfare of the people.
3. They provide a link between the government and the people.
4. They articulate and aggregate the interests of different sections of society.
5. They socialize and mobilize citizens.
6. They provide leadership and recruit political leaders.

notes.title: Challenges Faced by Political Parties
notes.question: What are the challenges faced by political parties?
notes.qnaAnswer:
1. Lack of internal democracy.
2. Dynastic succession.
3. Money and muscle power.
4. Lack of meaningful choice for voters.
5. Criminalization of politics.
6. Lack of ideological commitment.

notes.title: Q. Set 1 : Choose the Correct Option from Given Options and Complete the Statements

entries.question:
(1) The Election Commissioner is appointed by the ______.
(a) President
(b) Prime Minister
(c) Speaker of Lok Sabha
(d) Vice President
entries.answer: President. (Appointed under Article 324 of the Constitution.)

entries.question:
(2) ______ was appointed as the first Chief Election Commissioner of independent India.
(a) Sukumar Sen
(b) T. N. Seshan
(c) K. V. K. Sundaram
(d) Dr. Nagendra Singh
entries.answer: Sukumar Sen. (Administered India's mammoth first general elections in 1951–52.)

entries.question:
(3) Constituencies are created and restructured by the ______ Committee of the Election Commission.
(a) Selection
(b) Delimitation
(c) Voting
(d) Timetable
entries.answer: Delimitation. (The Delimitation Commission restructures parliamentary and assembly boundaries based on census migration data.)

entries.question:
(4) ______ from Himachal Pradesh was the first voter of independent India.
(a) Sham Sharan Negi
(b) Sukumar Sen
(c) T. N. Seshan
(d) K. C. Pant
entries.answer: Sham Sharan Negi. (Cast the first vote on 25th October 1951 in Kinnaur, Himachal Pradesh.)

notes.title: Q. Set 2 : State Whether the Following Statements are True or False, Giving Reasons

entries.question: (1) Under special circumstances, the Election Commission holds elections in a particular constituency for a second time.
entries.answer:
The statement is True.
Reasons:
(1) The Election Commission is constitutionally empowered to ensure free, fair, and credible elections.
(2) If reports of booth capturing, violence, or EVM tampering occur, the Commission cancels voting and orders repolling.
(3) If a sitting representative dies or resigns, mid-term bye-elections are conducted in that constituency.

entries.question: (2) The state government decides when and in how many stages elections would be held in a particular state.
entries.answer:
The statement is False.
Reasons:
(1) Under Article 324, the superintendence, direction, and control of all elections is vested exclusively in the Election Commission of India.
(2) If state governments managed election schedules, ruling parties might manipulate dates to their political advantage.
(3) As an autonomous constitutional body, the Election Commission independently decides polling dates, stages, and phases.

notes.title: Q. Set 3 : Explain the Concepts / Write Short Notes

entries.question: (1) Reorganising the Constituencies (Delimitation Commission):
entries.answer:
(1) The total number of members in Lok Sabha is 543, with each member representing one geographic constituency.
(2) Over decades, demographic migration from rural areas to urban centers altered voter populations significantly across regions.
(3) The Delimitation Commission, an independent sub-committee of the Election Commission, restructures constituency boundaries to equalize voter counts.
(4) It functions strictly without bowing to political influence or executive interference.

entries.question: (2) Mid-Term Elections:
entries.answer:
(1) If an elected government loses its parliamentary majority before completing its full five-year term due to the withdrawal of support by coalition partners, and no alternative coalition can form a government, the house is dissolved.
(2) In such situations, the Election Commission conducts mid-term general elections before the expiration of the full five-year tenure.
(3) Mid-term elections restore democratic mandates and governance stability.

entries.question: (3) Model Code of Conduct:
entries.answer:
(1) The Model Code of Conduct is a set of guidelines issued by the Election Commission to regulate political parties and candidates during election season.
(2) It takes effect the moment election dates are announced and remains in force until results are declared.
(3) It bars ruling parties from using government vehicles, advertising official schemes, or announcing financial grants to influence voters.
(4) It ensures that campaigns remain peaceful, fair, and ethical.

notes.title: Q. Set 4 : Do as Directed (Flowcharts & Concept Maps)

entries.question: Prepare a Flowchart showing the Process of Elections in India.
entries.answer:
1. Delimitation and establishment of Constituencies

2. Finalization and updating of Voters' Lists

3. Nomination of Candidates and Scrutiny of Application Forms

4. Election Campaigning across constituencies

5. Actual Voting (Polling via EVM & VVPAT)

6. Counting of Votes

7. Declaration of Election Results

8. Resolution of Election Disputes by Election Commission

entries.question: Complete the concept map: Stakeholders and Roles in the Electoral Process.
entries.answer:
• Role of Election Commission: Schedules dates, enforces Model Code, monitors polling, counts votes.
• Role of Political Parties: Select candidates, formulate policies and manifestos, conduct campaigns.
• Role of Candidates: File nomination affidavits, follow spending caps, present vision to voters.
• Role of Voters: Check names in electoral roll, turn out to vote fearlessly, use VVPAT to verify ballot.

notes.title: Q. Set 5 : Answer the Following in Brief

entries.question: (1) Explain the functions and powers of the Election Commission of India.
entries.answer:
(1) Preparing & Updating Electoral Rolls: Enrolls all eligible citizens who reach 18 years of age and issues Voter Identity Cards (EPIC).
(2) Election Timetables: Formulates complete polling schedules, phases, and booth allocations.
(3) Scrutiny of Nominations: Examines candidates' affidavits, educational qualifications, asset disclosures, and criminal antecedents.
(4) Recognition of Political Parties: Grants national or regional status to parties and allocates exclusive election symbols.
(5) Resolving Disputes: Acts as a quasi-judicial body to resolve electoral disputes, disqualify corrupt candidates, and order repolling where irregularities occur.

entries.question: (2) Explain the major Electoral Reforms required to strengthen Indian democracy.
entries.answer:
(1) Curbing Criminalisation: Legally barring candidates facing serious criminal charges from contesting elections.
(2) Controlling Money Power: Enforcing state funding of election expenses and imposing strict audits on party expenditure.
(3) Women's Representation: Enacting statutory 33% or 50% reservation for female candidates in Parliament and State Assemblies.
(4) Technological Security: Utilizing modern Electronic Voting Machines (EVM) coupled with Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) systems.
(5) Internal Party Democracy: Mandating transparent internal elections and financial audits for all recognized parties.
